title: Binding of gp37 LTF needle trimers to E. coli
author: Mohammad Z. Islam

steps_raw.instruction: Binding of gp37 LTF needle trimers to E. coli
Take freshly grown 108 E. coli cells and centrifuge at 2,300 g for 3 min at 4°C in a low-bind Eppendorf tube.
Resuspend the cells in phosphate buffer saline (PBS; pH 7.4) and add purified his-tagged gp37 LTF needle trimers at about 3 x 105 molecules per cell in a reaction volume of 150 µl.
Sediment the E. coli cells by centrifugation at 2,300 g for 3 min at 4°C followed by washing twice with 1 ml of PBS.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 µl PBS, transfer to a new tube, and add 10 µl of 2X SDS sample buffer.
Denature the protein by boiling for 7 min.
Perform Western blotting. First, transfer the proteins to a polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF) membrane.

After blocking with casein blocking buffer (Sigma Aldrich, St. Louis, MO) buffer or 5% skim milk in PBS containing 0.05% Tween 20 (PBS-T), incubate the membrane with monoclonal anti-histag antibodies (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA) at 37ºC for 2 hr to detect the bound his-tagged gp37 protein.
After washing four times with PBS-T, add horseradish peroxidase (HRP)-conjugated rabbit anti-mouse IgG (Invitrogen, Camarillo, CA), and incubate for 1 hour at 37ºC.
After washing four times with PBS-T, add the ECL reagent (Pierce Biotechnology, Rockford, IL).
Expose the membrane to an X-ray film or image with Chemidoc (Bio-Rad laboratories).
In each experiment, include two negative controls: (i) omission of gp37, and (ii) omission of E. coli cells.
